questions.question: Out of his monthly income, Mr. Sharma spends 24% on house rent and 70% on household expenses and saves the balance. If every month, he saves ₹1,200, then what is his monthly income?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

House rent = 24%

Household expenses = 70%

Savings = ₹1,200

**Formula used:**

Total monthly income = Savings ÷ (1 - (House rent percentage + Household expenses percentage))

**Calculation:**

Total monthly income = ₹1,200 ÷ (1 - (24% + 70%))

⇒ Total monthly income = ₹1,200 ÷ (1 - 0.94)

⇒ Total monthly income = ₹1,200 ÷ 0.06

⇒ Total monthly income = ₹20,000

**∴ The correct answer is option (1).**

questions.question: I walk at a speed of 10 km/h and reach my destination in 2 hrs. If I increase my speed by 2 km/h, how early would I reach my destination?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Speed = 10 km/h

Time = 2 hrs

New Speed = 10 + 2 = 12 km/h

**Formula used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

New Time = Distance ÷ New Speed

Time Saved = Original Time - New Time

**Calculation:**

Distance = 10 × 2 = 20 km

New Time = 20 ÷ 12 = 5/3 hrs

⇒ New Time = 5/3 hrs = (5/3 × 60) min = 100 min

Time Saved = 120 min - 100 min = 20 min

**∴ The correct answer is option (4).**

questions.question:
The ratio of the radius of the base and the perpendicular height of a right circular cone is given as 3 : 4 and the curved surface area of the cone is given as 2310 cm².

Find the radius (in cm) of the base of the given cone. (Use pi = (22)/(7) )
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The ratio of the radius of the base (r) and the perpendicular height (h) of a right circular cone = 3:4

Curved surface area = 2310 cm²

**Formula used:**

Curved Surface Area = π × r × l

Where, l = slant height

Using Pythagoras theorem: l = √(r² + h²)

**Calculations:**

Let radius (r) = 3k and height (h) = 4k

Slant height (l) = √(r² + h²)

⇒ l = √((3k)² + (4k)²)

⇒ l = √(9k² + 16k²)

⇒ l = 5k

Curved Surface Area = π × r × l

⇒ 2310 = (22/7) × 3k × 5k

⇒ 2310 = (22/7) × 15k²

⇒ 2310 = (330/7) × k²

⇒ k² = 49

⇒ k = 7

Radius (r) = 3k

⇒ r = 3 × 7 = 21 cm

**∴ The correct answer is option (1).**

questions.question: In a stationary shop, a pen is marked as ₹80 and it is sold at a discount of 15%. The shopkeeper also offers a special discount of ₹8 on the pen. Find the cost price of the pen if the shopkeeper earns a profit of 20%.

Marked Price (MP) = ₹80

Discount = 15%

Special Discount = ₹8

Profit = 20%

**Formula used:**

Selling Price (SP) = MP × (1 - Discount%) - Special Discount

Cost Price (CP) = SP × (1 / (1 + Profit%))

**Calculation:**

SP = ₹80 × (1 - 15/100) - ₹8

⇒ SP = ₹80 × 0.85 - ₹8

⇒ SP = ₹68 - ₹8 = ₹60

CP = ₹60 × (1 / (1 + 20/100))

⇒ CP = ₹60 × (1 / 1.2)

⇒ CP = ₹50

**∴ The correct answer is option (4).**

• **Bicameralism** refers to a legislative system in which there are two houses or chambers. In the context of India, these are the **Lok Sabha** (Lower House) and the **Rajya Sabha** (Upper House).
 
• This feature is considered **federal in nature** as it allows representation of the states in the legislative process through the **Rajya Sabha**, ensuring that the interests of the states are taken into account.
 
• The **Indian Constitution** under Article 79 provides for a bicameral legislature at the union level, which is a hallmark of a federal system.
 
• While not all states in India have bicameral legislatures, certain states like **Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Bihar, Karnataka, and Andhra Pradesh** also have bicameral systems. This reinforces the federal principle of shared legislative powers.
 
• Bicameralism ensures a system of **checks and balances**, preventing hasty legislation and protecting the interests of diverse groups, especially in a country as vast and varied as India.

• **Single Citizenship**__

• This promotes the idea of **national unity** and is considered a **unitary feature** rather than a federal one.

questions.question: When a sailor jumps out of a rowing boat, the boat moves backwards. This represents:

__
 
• The phenomenon of the boat moving backward when a sailor jumps out is explained by **Newton's Third Law of Motion**.
 
• According to the Third Law, for every **action**, there is an equal and opposite **reaction**.
 
• When the sailor jumps forward out of the boat, he exerts a forward force on the boat. The boat, in turn, exerts an equal and opposite backward force.
 
• This backward force causes the boat to move in the opposite direction (i.e., backward).
 
• The law is applied in various real-world scenarios such as the propulsion of rockets, movement of swimmers, and recoil of firearms.
 
• This law is fundamental in understanding the concept of **interaction forces**, where forces always occur in pairs.
 
• Newton's Third Law of Motion is a cornerstone of classical mechanics and is widely applicable in physics and engineering.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **First law of motion**__

 __
 
• **Newton's First Law of Motion**, also known as the **Law of Inertia**, states that an object will remain at rest or in uniform motion in a straight line unless acted upon by an external force.
 
• This law explains the concept of **inertia**, which is the resistance of an object to change its state of motion.
 
• It is not applicable in this scenario because the motion of the boat is due to interaction forces, not inertia.
 
 
 
• **Second law of motion**__
 __
 
• **Newton's Second Law of Motion** states that the force acting on an object is equal to the mass of the object multiplied by its acceleration (**F = ma**).
 
• This law primarily describes how forces influence the motion of an object.
 
• While the force exerted by the sailor may lead to acceleration, the scenario described is better explained by the Third Law.
 
 
 
• **Rectilinear motion**__
 
 
• **Rectilinear motion** refers to motion along a straight line.
 
• While the movement of the boat may occur along a straight path, the focus of the question is on the forces involved, making the Third Law the correct explanation.

__
 
• The original sentence "The dog is the most faithful animal" is in the **superlative degree**. It indicates that the dog possesses the quality of faithfulness to the highest degree among all animals.

 
 
• **Example:** Mount Everest is the highest peak in the world.
 
 
 
• To change a superlative sentence into the **positive degree**, we need to express the quality without comparison, or by comparing it equally with others, often using phrases like "as...as" or "so...as."
 
• Let's analyze the options:
 
 
• **1) The dog is more useful than any other animal.** This sentence is in the **comparative degree** ("more useful than") and changes the adjective from "faithful" to "useful," which is incorrect.
 
• **2) The dog is the faithful animal.** This sentence is in the **positive degree** but it doesn't convey the same level of faithfulness implied by the superlative. It simply states a fact without comparison.
 
• **3) No other animal is as faithful as the dog.** This sentence correctly converts the superlative into the positive degree. It uses the "as...as" structure to state that no other animal possesses the quality of faithfulness to the same extent as the dog, thereby implying the dog's supreme faithfulness without using the superlative form.
 
 
• **Example:** No other city is as beautiful as Paris. (Converting "Paris is the most beautiful city.")
 
 
 
• **4) The dog is the only faithful animal.** This sentence expresses an exclusive statement, which is a different meaning from the original superlative statement. While it suggests high faithfulness, it's not the standard conversion to the positive degree.
 
 
 
• Therefore, "No other animal is as faithful as the dog" is the most accurate transformation to the positive degree while retaining the original meaning of the dog's superior faithfulness.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 3**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Positive Degree:** Used to describe a quality without comparison (e.g., *faithful*, *big*, *happy*).
 
• **Comparative Degree:** Used to compare two things (e.g., *more faithful than*, *bigger than*, *happier than*).
 
• **Superlative Degree:** Used to compare three or more things, indicating the highest or lowest degree of a quality (e.g., *most faithful*, *biggest*, *happiest*).
 
 
 
• **Transforming Superlative to Positive:**
 
 
• **Rule:** When converting a superlative degree sentence (e.g., "X is the most ADJECTIVE Y") to a positive degree, start with "No other Y is as ADJECTIVE as X" or "No other Y is so ADJECTIVE as X."
